## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** no issues found in the tested scope. The four removed bindings are redundant, because Qt's `Column` positioner skips children with `visible: false` (and their spacing) whatever their height. Removing them eliminates the reported binding-loop warnings, and in visible states the panel layout stays the same.

In a synthetic Qt Quick fixture built from the verbatim base and head delegate blocks, with the real `PanelSectionHeader` and `PanelSeparator`, the results were:

| Removed binding (base line) | Base | Head |
|---|---|---|
| Network section header (`network/Panel.qml:1627`) | binding-loop warning | none |
| Network status `Text` (`network/Panel.qml:1921`) | binding-loop warning | none |
| Bluetooth section header (`bluetooth/Panel.qml:850`) | binding-loop warning | none |
| Bluetooth separator (`bluetooth/Panel.qml:844`) | no warning in any run | none |

- **Verified:** the Bluetooth header shows the same loop as the network header, so the Bluetooth half of the change, which the PR description says was checked only by inspection, is covered as well.
- **Verified:** in every visible state, base and head produced the same delegate heights, `ListView` `contentHeight`, single-line rows without status, and elided long status text. The only geometry differences appeared while an ancestor item was hidden, when nothing is on screen.
- The warning locations quoted in #11099 (`Panel.qml` lines 1513 and 1804 in the shipped 4.0.3/4.0.4 file) are these same two network bindings.

### Commit message describes a different mechanism than the one observed

The commit message attributes the warnings to a cycle through the delegate (`Item.height -> delegateColumn.implicitHeight -> child heights -> child.height -> child.implicitHeight`) and to `elide` on the status line. It also says a sibling can resolve to height 0. Qt 6.11.2 source and the fixture point elsewhere:

```text
Text { height: visible ? implicitHeight : 0 }   // created hidden, or status text empty
  -> later becomes visible (or gets its first status)
  -> height binding reads implicitHeight for the first time
  -> QQuickText computes implicit size lazily, inside that read
  -> implicitHeightChanged re-enters the same height binding -> warning
```

- The loop is local to each `Text`. It reproduced with a standalone `Text`, with no `Column` or delegate around it. The delegate chain above only flows one way (child to parent), so it is not a cycle.
- `elide` is not required: `PanelSectionHeader` has no elide and loops too.
- The separator is a `Rectangle` with a constant `implicitHeight`, so its binding is harmless redundancy rather than a loop source.
- In the fixture, base heights were correct after settling. No sibling ended up at height 0.

**Impact:** the code change is unaffected. The history would record an explanation that does not match the actual cause.

**Suggested change:** describe the cause as a `Text` whose own `height` binding is the first reader of its lazily computed `implicitHeight`. Describe the separator line as redundant cleanup, and drop the order-dependent height claim, or scope it to the cloned-panel observation.

**Stale code comment:** the status `Text` in `NetworkRow` still says it "Collapses to zero height when empty". The item now keeps its implicit height and the `Column` skips it. Suggested wording: "Hidden when empty; Column skips invisible children, so rows without status keep a tight one-line look."

**Scope note on #11099:** the removed bindings only compute item heights. Neither technical assessment found a path from these bindings to the panel's network activation calls, so this change is not expected to affect the reconnect outages described in #11099. The PR wording does not auto-close that issue.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the pinned head and base, plus Qt 6.11.2 qtdeclarative/qtbase and Quickshell v0.3.1 source. The runtime evidence comes from an isolated synthetic fixture run under the `qml` tool with the offscreen software backend: 36 base/head runs across three font families and two scales. Around the verbatim delegate blocks, the fixture stubs the style tokens, the outer row shells and all network and Bluetooth data. It did not run Quickshell, the real panels on a desktop, NetworkManager, BlueZ or `./test/all`, and the Qt version of the runtime was not recorded. The reconnect behavior in #11099 was assessed from source only.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments, with a targeted source follow-up to cross-check the mechanism, and an Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
